body:
## Signal

`packages/frontend/data/extendedBios.js:8273-8277` (FAQ, source of truth): *"Isaac Lamb's specific drum kit brand and model are not publicly documented. No official artist page or gear-focused interview naming his equipment has been found."* — repeated verbatim for cymbals, snare, and pedals. This is an explicit, deliberate "unverified" statement per CLAUDE.md's verified-only/omit-if-unsure rule, not a gap waiting to be filled.

`packages/frontend/data/albumArticles/isaac-lamb.js` fabricates specific brands across both entries anyway: `drumKit.brand` = "SJC Custom Drums" (lines 56, 314), `cymbals.brand` = "Meinl" (lines 96, 353), plus DW/Vic Firth/Evans in nested hardware fields (lines 145, 152, 159, 383) — none of these appear in any source cited by extendedBios, and no external verification is offered anywhere in this file. This is a stricter violation than the usual brand-drift class: the source of truth doesn't just disagree, it states the fact is unknowable from any source found so far.

## Fix

Two options, pick based on what's findable: (a) if a fresh source search finds Isaac Lamb's actual gear (his own social media, a gear-feature interview, Kublai Khan TX tour photos with a legible logo), update BOTH `extendedBios.js` and `albumArticles/isaac-lamb.js` consistently with that source cited; (b) if no verifiable source exists, strip the fabricated `"brand"`/model fields and specific-gear prose from `albumArticles/isaac-lamb.js` and replace with the same "not publicly documented" framing `extendedBios.js` already uses, rather than leaving invented brand names on a live page. Do not leave the fabricated brands in place either way — that violates the verified-only rule regardless of which file is "authoritative."

## Verify

1. `grep -n "\"brand\"" packages/frontend/data/albumArticles/isaac-lamb.js` → either replaced with a newly-verified-and-cited brand, or removed/hedged to match extendedBios's "not publicly documented" framing.
2. If a new source was found, confirm the citation URL is live (curl 200) and confirm `extendedBios.js` was updated to match, not just `albumArticles.js`.
3. No brand name appears in `albumArticles/isaac-lamb.js` that isn't backed by a cited source.

## Done

`albumArticles/isaac-lamb.js` either cites a genuine verified source for Isaac Lamb's gear (synced with `extendedBios.js`) or honestly states the gear is not publicly documented, matching `extendedBios.js` — no fabricated brand names remain on a live page.
title: SEO: Isaac Lamb albumArticles.js fabricates specific gear brands — extendedBios explicitly says gear is unverified/not publicly documented
